question.text: An atom absorbs a photon of wavelength <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>500</mn><mo> </mo><mi>nm</mi></math> and emits another photon of wavelength <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>600</mn><mo> </mo><mi>nm</mi></math>. The net energy absorbed by the atom in this process is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mi>eV</mi></math>. The value of<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo> </mo><mi>n</mi><mo> </mo></math>is [Assume the atom to be stationary during the absorption and emission process] (Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>34</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"/> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>8</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> ).

solution.text:
The energy of a photon is given by E=hcλ.

It is given that λ1=500 nm, λ2=600 nm.

The net energy absorbed is 

ΔE=hcλ1-hcλ2=hc10-9(1500-1600)

=6.6×10-34×3×108×100500×600×10-9

=6.6×330×10-19 J

1 eV=1.6×10-19 J

=6.6×330×1.6eV

=4125×10-4 eV
